problems.problem: Contact detail crop [386,1170,974,1420] confirms a real contact shadow at the base line (offset_y 0 is correct, do not move it), but it is a thin dark sliver roughly x 500-760 versus the 428px bottle footprint and reads faint at poster scale. More critically, below y=1310 the render shows only continuous vertical troweled plaster with no horizontal support plane, no tonal shift and no cast-shadow spread, so the eye reads a vertical wall and the bottle appears pasted onto it instead of standing on the declared interior ledge.

The arched recess no longer frames the hero: the niche now sits left of the bottle (opening approx x 300-490, y 360-1130) with its ledge at y~1100, about 210px above the bottle base at y=1310, so the bottle stands beside the arch instead of 'at the arch heart' per the declared concept, and the niche's right jamb runs as a hard tangent along the bottle's left silhouette. Plaster value also renders as a mid clay-orange lighter than the declared saturated #b0562f, softening the warm-earth vs dark-glass temperature contrast and leaving the cream hairline rule at (76,353) low-contrast.

The left type column still occupies only y=86-353 while the bottle spans y=360-1310, so the lower ~65% of the left column is empty plaster; the asymmetric two-column grid loses its vertical counterweight and the eye drops from the title into dead space. The proposed title.y/subtitle.y moves from the last critique are not present in the current render (title bbox still [76,158,738,208]), so this weakness is unchanged. References (Terre d'Hermès, Armani Privé) keep type and product in continuous dialogue across the frame.

Hierarchy inside the masthead is flat: logo 28px, title 72px and subtitle 22px are all the same dark brown #261E16 in the same roman Times cut with wide vertical gaps (logo baseline ~105, title 158-208, subtitle 288-303), so the column reads as three disconnected lines rather than one locked block, and the dark ink fights the declared cream #f6ead9 type voice of the concept against the clay ground.

changes.value: Hand-troweled sun-baked terracotta clay plaster wall in saturated burnt-orange ochre, one wide shallow vertical arched recess centered in the right two thirds of the frame spanning from upper third down to a horizontal plaster ledge plane in the lower fifth, ledge surface catching soft frontal daylight with a gentle value fall-off and faint cast shading beneath anything placed upon it, broad soft frontal light with warm ambient bounce, fine trowel ridges, empty scene, no objects
